strategic_horizon.terminal_goal: Build a personal cross-platform VPN whose logical weak-network behavior approaches UDP/QUIC while public carriers remain stock REALITY/Vision over real kernel TCP.
strategic_horizon.current_milestone: M10 UDP/QUIC oracle and realistic network-profile benchmark harness
strategic_horizon.local_optimization_stop_rule: Do not freeze a production FEC wire frame, modify REALITY/Vision, or start TUN/platform integration until M10 reproduces M9 protection candidates against native TCP/UDP and a pinned QUIC oracle across realistic loss/stall/reorder profiles. Include a bounded soft-deadline/tail-recovery candidate because M9 proved GAP-only recovery cannot detect a missing final extent.

continuation_cursor.last_completed_action: Completed M9-001 at substantive commit b06a0fdcb0c502cfa2584b71cba4dc808fe70269: added a deterministic same-budget protection harness around the M8 RBC ledger and compared M6-style reactive reinjection, proactive duplication, and minimal pairwise XOR repair at 1.5x and 2.0x. XOR showed a repeatable one-step advantage for isolated stalls and bursts split across repair groups at 1.5x, but failed badly when two stalled chunks were in the same XOR pair; full 2.0x duplication remained the latency ceiling in the simplified model. An exhaustive 1.5x single-stall sweep also quantified a separate M6 limitation: a stalled final STREAM chunk/FIN cannot be discovered by GAP_HINT alone because no later offset exists. FEC is experimentally admitted but production-deferred. Local vet, normal/race tests, protocol fuzz (~148k executions), Linux/386, Linux/mipsle and Windows/amd64 experiment cross-builds, handoff verification and continuity tests passed.
continuation_cursor.current_task: M10-001: build the first local benchmark/profile harness that measures native TCP, native UDP, and WBD protection candidates under reproducible delay/stall/reorder schedules; define the QUIC oracle dependency/pin without allowing it to block the initial local baseline.
continuation_cursor.why_now: M9 established that protection choice is workload/fault-shape dependent and exposed a tail-gap blind spot. The project now needs measurements closer to real transport behavior before choosing FEC, duplication, reinjection timers, or RBC allocation policy.
continuation_cursor.done_when: A local sandbox benchmark harness has versioned network profiles and repeatable seeds, records p50/p95/p99 logical delivery or recovery latency plus intentional bytes, includes native TCP and UDP baselines and WBD reinjection/duplicate/XOR candidates, explicitly exercises final-chunk/tail stalls with a bounded soft-deadline recovery candidate, and records a pinned plan for adding a QUIC oracle. No REALITY/Vision, TUN, public wire-format or platform-specific changes yet.
continuation_cursor.next_atomic_action: M10-001: add a deterministic benchmark profile/result schema and a local socket/fault-proxy harness for native TCP and UDP plus WBD candidate runs. Start with fixed clean, reordered, single-stall, burst-stall and final-chunk-stall profiles; add a bounded soft-deadline reinjection candidate so the M9 tail blind spot is measurable. Keep QUIC as the next substep unless a pinned implementation is already locally available.
